The reasoning is sound and the answer 1305 is correct.

Divisors $d \ge n/100$ pair with divisors $n/d \le 100$, so the number of divisors at least $n/100$ equals $t$, the number of divisors of $M$ that are at most 100. The imbalance condition becomes $d(M) > 100t$.

Since $100 \mid 2000 \mid M$, the 13 divisors of 2000 that are at most 100 all divisor $M$, so $t \ge 13$ and $d(M) \ge 1301$.

If $t = 13$, then $2^5 = 32$ cannot divide $M$, so the exponent of 2 is exactly 4. This makes $5 \mid d(M)$, so $d(M) \ge 1305$. Since $t \ge 14$ forces $d(M) > 1400$, no smaller value is possible.

The value 1305 is achieved by $M = 2^4 \cdot 5^{28} \cdot 101^2 \cdot 103^2$. Here $d(M) = 5 \cdot 29 \cdot 9 = 1305$, and the only divisors at most 100 are the 13 divisors of 2000, so $t = 13$. Then $1305 > 1300$ holds, and $1292/1305 \approx 0.99004 > 0.99$.
